reasons: Composio's managed Gmail app is already verified by Google, so you can ship to real users without any review on your side. The trade-off is that your users see 'Composio' on Google's consent screen, and only your own OAuth app can change that.

Managed auth uses a fixed scope set, full mailbox access (https://mail.google.com/), and cannot add scopes such as gmail.settings.basic for filter tools. Users on the managed app who need an extra scope hit Google's 'app is blocked' screen.

Gmail API quotas are counted per Google Cloud project. On the managed app you share Composio's project quota with every other Composio customer. Google is also adding a daily billing threshold of 80,000,000 quota units per project, with charges above it. Your own project gives you your own quota.

Bringing your own app with the same full-mailbox scope means restricted-scope verification plus a paid CASA security assessment every 12 months. Plan for weeks, not days, unless you cut the scopes down to send-only or keep the app internal to your Workspace organization.

Composio's docs disagree on the redirect URI: the Google credentials guide shows the /api/v1/auth-apps/add path, and the custom auth config docs show /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback and say the v1 path is still supported. Copy the one your auth config shows.

verdict.summary: Heavy verification. The Composio Gmail toolkit asks for full mailbox access (https://mail.google.com/), a restricted scope. Your own app with that scope needs brand verification, restricted-scope review with a demo video, and a paid third-party CASA security assessment that you redo every year. Google says this can take several weeks. Cheaper paths: a send-only app (gmail.send, sensitive) skips CASA and Google says review typically takes 3-5 business days. An Internal app used only inside your own Workspace organization needs no verification. Or keep using Composio's managed app, which is already verified.

timeToProduction.label: 2-12 weeks for restricted scopes. Google says 'several weeks' and warns it can take months. Send-only (gmail.send): 3-5 business days per Google

verdict.mainBlocker: Restricted-scope verification: a demo video, scope justifications and a privacy policy that meets Google's Limited Use rules, then a CASA security assessment by a Google-approved lab, renewed every 12 months. Until you are verified, the unverified-app screen shows and you are capped at 100 new users.

stages.name: Create the Google Cloud project and OAuth client
limits: Every domain you use anywhere in the project (homepage, privacy policy, redirect URI) must be added as an authorized domain first.
Redirect URIs must be HTTPS and match the request exactly, including trailing slash.

steps.title: Create a project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In the Google Cloud console, create a new project for production. Google recommends separate projects for testing and production. Then open APIs & Services > Library, search for Gmail API and enable it. If you skip this, Composio tool calls fail with 'Gmail API has not been used in project'.
steps.humanReason: Requires signing in to your Google account and accepting Google Cloud terms.

links.label: Gmail API in the API Library

steps.title: Fill in Branding and Audience
steps.detail: Open Google Auth Platform > Branding. Enter the app name your users will see, a user support email you monitor, a logo (square, 120x120 px), your homepage and privacy policy URLs, and your authorized domain. The homepage must be on a domain you own, describe what the app does (not just a login page) and link to the privacy policy. Then open Audience and choose External for any Google user, or Internal if only people in your own Google Workspace organization will connect (Internal apps need no verification).
steps.humanReason: Inside your signed-in Cloud console. The app name, support email and policy links are statements your company makes to Google.

preparedValues.label: App name
preparedValues.value: <Your product name> (must not include Google product names like 'Gmail')

preparedValues.label: Limited Use statement for your site
preparedValues.value: The use of information received from Google Workspace scopes will adhere to the Google User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

steps.title: Declare scopes on the Data Access page
steps.detail: Open Data Access and add only the scopes your agent's tools need. Google groups them as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted, and the group decides your verification path. The scopes you request at runtime must match what you declare here, or users see the unverified-app screen. Do not combine gmail.metadata with a content scope: Composio notes they are incompatible in one request.

preparedValues.label: Same as Composio managed (restricted, needs CASA)
Read, label and send without permanent delete (restricted, needs CASA)

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: Open Clients > Create client, choose Web application and paste Composio's redirect URI under Authorized redirect URIs. Copy it from your Composio auth config, do not type it from a guide: Composio's own pages show two different paths. The redirect domain must also be an authorized domain, and for verification you must prove you own every authorized domain, which you cannot do for Composio's domain. If you plan to verify, route the callback through your own domain (Composio documents a redirect proxy) and register that URI here instead. Then create a client secret and copy the Client ID and Secret.
steps.humanReason: Inside your signed-in console. The secret should only pass from Google to Composio.

links.label: Composio: route the callback through your domain

preparedValues.label: Authorized redirect URI
preparedValues.value: Copy from Composio: Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Gmail > OAuth2 > Use your own developer credentials

preparedValues.label: Redirect URI if you proxy through your domain

stages.name: Connect it in Composio and test
limits: Testing status allows at most 100 test users, and each must be added by email.
In Testing, refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent, so every connection dies after a week and the user must reconnect.
Test users see a warning screen before consent.

steps.title: Add yourself as a test user
steps.detail: Leave Publishing status on Testing and add your own Google account (and any teammates) under Audience > Test users.

steps.title: Create the Gmail auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create a Gmail auth config with OAuth2 and your own credentials: Client ID, Client Secret, and the same scopes you declared on the Data Access page, passed in credentials.scopes. Make sure the redirect URI in the auth config is the exact one you registered in Google.

steps.title: Connect your own Gmail and run one tool
steps.detail: Start a connection, click through the test-user warning, approve the consent screen and run a read tool (for example, GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS) or a send tool to confirm it works. Users can untick scopes on Google's consent screen, and Composio still marks the connection active, so check that the tool you need actually works.
steps.humanReason: You approve Google's consent screen with your own account.

stages.name: Verify your brand and domain

duration.label: Minutes if the automated check passes, 2-3 business days if it goes to manual review

limits: A passed brand check is valid for 7 days. Publish it in that window or run it again.
You cannot request scope verification until branding is published.

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Search Console
steps.detail: Using a Google account that is an Owner or Editor on the Cloud project, verify every authorized domain in Google Search Console, usually with a DNS TXT record.
steps.humanReason: Needs DNS access for your domain and your Google sign-in.

steps.title: Run Verify Branding and publish
steps.detail: On the Branding page click Verify Branding. The automated check usually finishes in minutes. If it passes, click Publish branding within 7 days. If it fails, fix the listed issues or ask for a manual review.

stages.name: Publish and pass scope verification

duration.label: Restricted scopes: 2-12 weeks including CASA. Sensitive only: 3-5 business days per Google

limits: Until verified, the unverified-app screen shows and the app can take 100 new users in total.
Restricted scopes need a CASA security assessment from a Google-approved lab, paid by you, renewed at least every 12 months.
Adding a new restricted scope later can mean a fresh assessment.
You may not use Gmail data to train AI models beyond that user's own personalized model.

steps.title: Switch Publishing status to In production
steps.detail: On the Audience page click Publish app. Any Google user can now connect, but with sensitive or restricted scopes they see the unverified-app screen and you are capped at 100 new users until verification completes.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record an English screen capture that shows the full consent flow, the app name on the consent screen, your OAuth client ID in the browser address bar, and every feature that uses each sensitive or restricted scope. Upload it to YouTube as Unlisted. Google adds that task automation platforms must show how workflows are created and which way user data flows, which is how many agent products will be read.
steps.humanReason: The agent can write the script and shot list; a person has to record it with a real account and upload it to YouTube.

steps.title: Submit the data access request
steps.detail: In the Verification Center, pick your permitted application type, justify each scope and say why a narrower scope is not enough, and paste the video link. Gmail's approved use cases include email clients, backup, productivity tools (including generative AI summaries) and reporting that benefits the user. Bulk unsolicited mail is prohibited, and in 2026 a developer reported a send-only app rejected on that ground, so explain who receives the mail and why they asked for it. Google's Trust & Safety team replies only by email to the support and developer contact addresses, so keep those current.
steps.humanReason: A legal submission on behalf of your company.

preparedValues.label: Scope justification starter
preparedValues.value: Our AI assistant reads, labels and replies to the signed-in user's email on their instruction. It needs <scope> because <feature> reads message bodies; gmail.send alone cannot read mail.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: Google's Trust & Safety team emails you when it is time to start. Pick an App Defense Alliance authorized lab. Google, not you, decides whether you need assurance level AL1 or AL2. The lab tests the app, its infrastructure and wherever user data is stored, and issues a Letter of Validation. Plan to meet Google's restricted-scope security rules too: tokens encrypted at rest, keys in a key management system, and prompt injection protection (Google names its Model Armor or an equivalent). Developers report self-serve lab prices from about $540.
steps.humanReason: A paid contract with a third-party lab, and scans that need access to your code and infrastructure.

steps.title: Diary the annual recertification
steps.detail: Restricted-scope apps must pass a new, full CASA assessment every 12 months from the previous Letter of Validation, whether or not the app changed. Google emails the project Owners and Editors when it is due.

requirements.title: A domain you own, with homepage and privacy policy on it
requirements.detail: The homepage must describe the app and link to the privacy policy, both on a domain verified in Search Console. Every domain in the project, including the redirect URI's, must be an authorized domain.

requirements.title: Privacy policy that meets Limited Use
requirements.detail: It must say how the app accesses, uses, stores and shares Google user data, and your site must carry a Limited Use statement. Gmail data may not be sold, used for ads, or used to train AI models beyond that user's personalized model.

requirements.title: An approved Gmail use case
requirements.detail: Gmail scopes are only granted for approved use cases such as email clients, backup, productivity features (Google names generative AI summaries) and user-benefiting reporting.

requirements.title: Annual CASA assessment for restricted scopes
requirements.detail: Required if restricted Gmail data is stored on or passes through a server, which is the case when Composio runs the tools. Renewed every 12 months.

requirements.title: Security controls for restricted data
requirements.detail: Google lists HTTPS in transit, tokens encrypted at rest, keys in an HSM or equivalent key management system, and prompt injection protection.

blockers.title: redirect_uri_mismatch
blockers.symptom: Google shows 'Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch' before the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Make the Authorized redirect URI in Google identical to the one in your Composio auth config, scheme, case and trailing slash included. Copy it from the Composio dashboard; its docs show both a /api/v1/ and a /api/v3/ path.

blockers.title: Connections die after 7 days
blockers.symptom: Tool calls fail with auth errors about a week after a user connected.
blockers.fix: The app is still in Testing, where refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent. Publish the app to In production; users then reconnect once.

blockers.title: Unverified app screen and the 100-user cap
blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app', and new users stop being able to connect after 100.
blockers.fix: Complete verification for the scopes you request. The cap counts new users in total, so do not burn it on a public launch before verification. Also check that the scopes your auth config requests match the Data Access page exactly.

blockers.title: 'App is blocked' after adding a scope
blockers.symptom: Google blocks the consent screen after you add a scope such as gmail.settings.basic.
blockers.fix: The scope is not verified for that OAuth client. Remove it, or add it to your own app's verification request. On Composio's managed app you cannot add scopes.

blockers.title: Customer's Workspace admin blocks the app
blockers.symptom: Users at a company tell you the app is blocked, or their existing connection stopped working.
blockers.fix: Their admin has restricted Gmail access or blocked unconfigured third-party apps. The admin must mark your OAuth client ID as Trusted (or Specific Google data) in Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls.

blockers.title: Verification stalls with no email
blockers.symptom: The Verification Center says 'under review' or 'pending CASA' for weeks, or rejects the form for a missing demo video you did submit.
blockers.fix: Check spam and the support and developer contact addresses, since Google only replies there. Developers in 2025-2026 reported waiting a week or more for the CASA email and a form bug that wiped scope justifications; resubmitting and replying in the existing email thread is the reported path.

blockers.title: Rate limit errors
blockers.fix: Each user gets 6,000 quota units a minute per project and messages.send costs 100 units, so about 60 sends a minute per user. Add backoff. On the managed app, the project quota is shared with other Composio customers.
